Title: Week 01: Audit GitHub/LinkedIn/CV
Technical / research work: Audit GitHub/LinkedIn/CV; create roadmap board; reserve weekly time blocks; define compute/hardware access.
Exit criterion: Public landing README, private tracker, baseline skills/compute inventory.
Relationship / public action: List 30 targets: 10 local, 10 PhD/early-career/maintainers, 5 peers, 5 senior people.

Title: Week 02: Refresh MDPs, value/policy methods, PPO/SAC
Technical / research work: Refresh MDPs, value/policy methods, PPO/SAC; implement or cleanly reproduce small Gymnasium baselines.
Exit criterion: Reproducible PPO/SAC runs, plots, environment lockfile, short learning note.
Relationship / public action: Follow relevant labs/maintainers; make two substantive comments based on actual papers/code.

Title: Week 03: Read 6 anchor papers: generalization/meta-RL, domain randomization, robust RL, sim-to-real, fault tolerance, chosen environment. Create literature matrix.
Technical / research work: Read 6 anchor papers: generalization/meta-RL, domain randomization, robust RL, sim-to-real, fault tolerance, chosen environment. Create literature matrix.
Exit criterion: One-page problem statement plus matrix of method/data/metric/limitation/open question.
Relationship / public action: Meet one UoM faculty member/project supervisor; ask for 20 minutes of critique, not a position.

Title: Week 04: Write a 2-page proposal: question, hypotheses, methods, perturbations, metrics, compute budget, risks. Run one pilot.
Technical / research work: Write a 2-page proposal: question, hypotheses, methods, perturbations, metrics, compute budget, risks. Run one pilot.
Exit criterion: Mentor-reviewed proposal and a go/no-go decision on environment/scope.
Relationship / public action: Contact a second local robotics/AI/control academic with the proposal attached.

Title: Week 05: Build environment wrapper and deterministic evaluation harness
Technical / research work: Build environment wrapper and deterministic evaluation harness; add action latency and observation noise.
Exit criterion: Unit tests; seeded rollouts; baseline environment video.
Relationship / public action: Open one well-researched issue only if you find a genuine reproducible problem.

Title: Week 06: Implement classical-control/reference baseline and logging pipeline.
Technical / research work: Implement classical-control/reference baseline and logging pipeline.
Exit criterion: Baseline controller evaluated across nominal and perturbed conditions.
Relationship / public action: Write a short technical note on the simulator/control assumptions.

Title: Week 07: Train nominal PPO and SAC using fixed budgets
Technical / research work: Train nominal PPO and SAC using fixed budgets; diagnose stability.
Exit criterion: Five-seed nominal baseline table; failures documented, not hidden.
Relationship / public action: Speak with one PhD student/maintainer working near the chosen tool or topic.

Title: Week 08: Build plotting/report pipeline
Technical / research work: Build plotting/report pipeline; package v0.1.
Exit criterion: Public milestone: setup instructions, first results, 60–90 second demo.
Relationship / public action: Progress post #1; ask for feedback on one specific technical decision.

Title: Week 09: Add fault injection: torque loss, stuck/biased actuator or payload/model mismatch.
Technical / research work: Add fault injection: torque loss, stuck/biased actuator or payload/model mismatch.
Exit criterion: Fault sweep across held-out severity levels.
Relationship / public action: Study Swilling/Bentzel public talks/posts; record three technical questions, send none yet unless artifact is relevant.

Title: Week 10: Implement curriculum/domain-randomized training.
Technical / research work: Implement curriculum/domain-randomized training.
Exit criterion: Curriculum variant trained with matched compute budget.
Relationship / public action: Submit a small robosuite/Gymnasium/SB3 docs/test/bug PR if ready.

Title: Week 11: Run controlled ablations
Technical / research work: Run controlled ablations; compare nominal, randomization, and curriculum.
Exit criterion: Preliminary ablation plots and written interpretation.
Relationship / public action: Mentor review #2; identify one realistic paper/workshop/student venue.

Title: Week 12: Midpoint replication and scope review. Cut weak extensions.
Technical / research work: Midpoint replication and scope review. Cut weak extensions.
Exit criterion: v0.2 release and 3-page midpoint report with limitations.
Relationship / public action: Send one value-first message to an accessible engineer/PhD student, linking the relevant result.

Title: Week 13: Freeze hypotheses, primary metrics, evaluation conditions, seed count, and exclusion rules.
Technical / research work: Freeze hypotheses, primary metrics, evaluation conditions, seed count, and exclusion rules.
Exit criterion: Versioned evaluation protocol committed before final runs.
Relationship / public action: Progress post #2; share protocol and invite methodological criticism.

Title: Week 14: Final experiment batch A: main method comparisons.
Technical / research work: Final experiment batch A: main method comparisons.
Exit criterion: Complete raw results with automatic provenance (config, commit, seed).
Relationship / public action: Offer a concise contribution to a local lab/student project where your control/embedded skill is useful.

Title: Week 15: Final experiment batch B: fault/severity generalization.
Technical / research work: Final experiment batch B: fault/severity generalization.
Exit criterion: Held-out perturbation results and confidence intervals.
Relationship / public action: Talk to one researcher whose paper you reproduced; lead with what you found.

Title: Week 16: Failure taxonomy and robustness analysis
Technical / research work: Failure taxonomy and robustness analysis; create rollout examples.
Exit criterion: At least 3 recurring failure modes with quantitative frequency and videos.
Relationship / public action: If relevant, message Scott Nguyen with a calibration/inspection-specific artifact and one focused question.

Title: Week 17: Add only one high-value extension: HIL, GRIP/SCARA validation, or safety constraint.
Technical / research work: Add only one high-value extension: HIL, GRIP/SCARA validation, or safety constraint.
Exit criterion: Extension complete or explicitly dropped by the end of the week.
Relationship / public action: Mentor review #3; ask whether results are submission-worthy.

Title: Week 18: Independent rerun from a clean environment
Technical / research work: Independent rerun from a clean environment; documentation and tests.
Exit criterion: Another person—or a clean machine—can reproduce one headline result.
Relationship / public action: Follow up with prior contacts by sharing the improved artifact, not “just checking in.”

Title: Week 19: Write paper: abstract, intro, related work, method, protocol.
Technical / research work: Write paper: abstract, intro, related work, method, protocol.
Exit criterion: Full skeleton with every figure/table placed and claims tied to evidence.
Relationship / public action: Ask 2 reviewers: one controls/robotics person and one ML person.

Title: Week 20: Write results, discussion, limitations, ethics/safety, reproducibility statement.
Technical / research work: Write results, discussion, limitations, ethics/safety, reproducibility statement.
Exit criterion: Complete draft v1; no placeholder results.
Relationship / public action: Progress post #3 focused on one honest insight or negative result.

Title: Week 21: Incorporate reviews
Technical / research work: Incorporate reviews; rerun only experiments necessary to resolve a real concern.
Exit criterion: Draft v2 plus response-to-feedback log.
Relationship / public action: If a result directly relates, send a concise artifact-based note to a relevant senior target; otherwise wait.

Title: Week 22: Release code/data allowed for release, project page, demo, and technical report/preprint.
Technical / research work: Release code/data allowed for release, project page, demo, and technical report/preprint.
Exit criterion: v1.0 repository, archived release/DOI if possible, 3–5 minute video, 6–8 page report.
Relationship / public action: Submit to a mentor-approved workshop/student/reproducibility venue if quality and timing fit.

Title: Week 23: Targeted outreach and applications packet.
Technical / research work: Targeted outreach and applications packet.
Exit criterion: Research résumé, academic CV, project one-pager, research statement paragraph, contact tracker.
Relationship / public action: Carefully contact 2–3 highly relevant people, each with a different, evidence-based reason.

Title: Week 24: Portfolio integration, mock interview, retrospective, next 6-month plan.
Technical / research work: Portfolio integration, mock interview, retrospective, next 6-month plan.
Exit criterion: Final dashboard; mock research talk; applications/opportunity list; next milestone chosen.
Relationship / public action: Thank contributors/reviewers; send updates to people who gave useful feedback.
